chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhassan ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The ring in the mouth of the fasting one is not a problem (does not break the fast), but as for the date-stone, then no (it breaks the fast).'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: It is not a problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does keeping a ring or a date stone in the mouth break the fast?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between objects that remain in the mouth versus those swallowed, ruling that a ring (khātam) does not invalidate the fast while a date stone (nawā) does, likely due to differences in size, texture, or likelihood of being swallowed. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that breaking the fast requires the actual consumption or swallowing of the object, not merely its presence in the oral cavity. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the nuances of *mubtilat al-sawm* (nullifiers of the fast) in Usuli jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Muhassan Bin Ahmad, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The ring in the mouth of the Fasting one, is not with a problem. But, as for the date-stone, so no’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘The presence of a signet in the mouth of a fasting person is not harmful, but a date-stone is.’”
